title: The open-complement condition is unconditional and uniform in the coefficient ring
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring
annihilated by a power of a prime $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$, let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and let
$T$ be a finite-type
$k$-scheme of dimension at most $d$, and let
$j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be a
quasi-compact open immersion.
Then the pair $(V,T)$ satisfies the open-complement condition of
[def-exc-open-complement-bound] with $c=2d$, and it does so for
*every* finite coefficient ring $A$ of that shape at once: both
clauses hold — the vanishing $R^qj_*M=0$ for every $q>2d$ and every
sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules on $V_{\Et}$, and the
constructibility of
$R^qj_*F$ in every degree for every constructible $A$-sheaf $F$ — and
the constant $2d$ depends on $T$ alone, not on $A$. In particular, in
the setting of the global finite-field datum with $k=\Fbar$ and at the
finite coefficient stages $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions], the
condition holds for every $n\geq1$ with the same constant $2d$; for the
chart complements $W_U\subseteq\mathbf A^{d_U}_B$ in the assembly
[thm-pur-general-admissibility] for a separated finite-type morphism
$X\to Y$ of finite-type $k$-schemes, discard empty affine chart bases
$B\subseteq Y$. For every remaining chart,
$d_U+\dim B\leq d_U+\dim Y$, and the condition holds with
$c_U=2(d_U+\dim B)$, again independent of $n$. Empty chart bases may
alternatively be retained with $c_U=0$, since their ambient scheme and
complement are empty. The special cases
recorded in [lem-exc-open-complement-known] — dimension zero, where an
open immersion of a zero-dimensional Noetherian scheme is also closed, and
dimension at most one, by
[thm-exc-curve-open-dimension-general], [thm-exc-curve-open-constructible-general]
— are independent computations of the same condition and are neither used
nor superseded here.
Here finite type, open immersion and dimension mean [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-open-immersion] and [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], respectively; separably closed has the meaning of [def-kun-separably-closed].

proof.text: Geometry of the open immersion. The quasi-compact open immersion $j$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. Its source is finite type over $k$: take a finite affine cover of $T$ from the definition of finite type. The inverse image of each member is quasi-compact by the hypothesis on $j$, and their finite union $V$ is quasi-compact (restrict an open cover to each member and combine the finitely many finite subcovers). By [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open], $V$ has a finite affine open cover. By [def-weil-open-immersion], those opens are also affine opens of $T$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to the structure morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that their coordinate rings are finitely generated $k$-algebras. Thus this cover witnesses that $V$ is finite type over $k$. The same definition identifies $V$ with its open image in $T$, and [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone], applied to $V\subseteq T$, gives $\dim V\leq\dim T\leq d$.

source.place: Proof Step 2: quasi-compact open immersion is finite type; Step 3: dimension of the open

proof.text: Constructibility. Choose an integer $r\geq1$ with $\ell^r A=0$, and put $N=\ell^r$. This integer is invertible in $k$, since $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$. Apply [thm-exc-direct-image-input-holds] to $k,N,A$. Unpack clause (1) of [def-exc-direct-image-input], and apply it to $j:V\to T$, whose source, target and morphism are finite type by step 1 and the hypotheses. For every constructible $A$-sheaf $F$, each $R^qj_*F$ is constructible for $q\geq0$. For negative degrees apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] with $b=0$, $L=F[0]$ and $v=j_*$. Its source and target categories of $A$-module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], applied to $V$ and $T$, and $j_*$ is additive and left exact by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus $R^qj_*F=0$ for $q<0$; the zero sheaf is constructible (use the single stratum $T$, on which it is the constant finite zero module). This supplies every degree required by the condition.

source.place: Proof Steps 1-2: direct-image input and its constructibility clause

proof.text: Vanishing. Use [lem-kun-relative-torsion-direct-image-dimension-bound], the existing general form of the finite-type torsion-cohomology argument over a separably closed field. Set its $X=V$, $Y=T$, $f=j$, $\Lambda=A$, and take the structure map $a_V$ to be $j$ followed by $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The required compatibility is then an identity. The hypothesis on $a_T$ follows from finite type, and $j$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type by step 1. The additive group of $A$ is torsion because $\ell^r$ kills every element. Finally $\dim V\leq d$ by step 1. The lemma therefore gives $R^qj_*M=0$ for every $A$-module sheaf $M$ and every $q>2d$, including nonconstructible $M$. No separatedness, properness or algebraic closedness in place of separable closedness is inserted. This invokes the already split generic dimension bound, rather than treating the strict-henselization formula alone as a neighbourhood-colimit theorem.

source.place: Proof Step 3: torsion cohomological dimension and vanishing of higher direct images

proof.text: Uniformity. Steps 2 and 3 prove precisely the two clauses of [def-exc-open-complement-bound] with $c=2d$. The integer $d$ was fixed before choosing $A$, and neither argument changes it. Since $A$ was arbitrary among the stated finite rings, the same $2d$ works for all of them. To choose a bound depending on $T$ alone, use $d=\dim T$ when $T$ is nonempty; this is a finite nonnegative integer by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. If $T$ is empty, use $d=0$; all the sheaf categories involved have only the zero sheaf, so both clauses hold.

source.place: Proof Step 4, first paragraph: coefficient independence of the constant

proof.text: Finite coefficient stages. In [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], $k$ is the algebraic closure of the finite field of characteristic $p$ and $\ell\neq p$. By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ is a finite commutative ring, $\mathfrak m_E=\{x:|x|_E<1\}=\varpi_E\mathcal O_E$, and the absolute value extends the $\ell$-adic one. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $|\ell|_E=|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}<1$. Thus $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E$, so $\ell=\varpi_E b$ for some $b\in\mathcal O_E$, and $\ell^n=\varpi_E^n b^n$ annihilates $A_{E,n}$. The general result already established applies for each $n\geq1$ with the same $2d$. This is ordinary small-etale sheaf cohomology at the finite coefficient ring; no pro-etale comparison is required for this assertion.

source.place: Proof Step 4, finite-field and A_{E,n} specialization

proof.text: Geometry and dimension of a chart complement. Fix a nonempty affine chart base $B=\operatorname{Spec}R$ in the stated assembly and put $m=d_U$. It is an affine open of the finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$, so $R$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] applied to the structure morphism of $Y$. By [def-sbc-affine-space], the ambient chart is $T_U=\mathbf A^m_B=\operatorname{Spec}R[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$. Both $R$ and the polynomial algebra are finitely generated over $k$ (append the $m$ variables to generators of $R$), so [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] makes them Noetherian and their spectra Noetherian topological spaces. Apply [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] to $R$ and the $m$ variables, and translate ring dimension to spectrum dimension using [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring]. This gives $\dim T_U=m+\dim B$, a finite nonnegative integer by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Also $\dim B\leq\dim Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone]. The complement $W_U$ of the closed chart is open, and its inclusion in $T_U$ is quasi-compact: in a space with descending chain condition on closed subsets every open cover of every open subset has a finite subcover (otherwise successively adjoining an open not covered by the preceding finite union gives a nonstationary ascending chain of opens). Apply this also to its intersection with any affine open of $T_U$. Thus the complement meets the quasi-compactness hypothesis of the general assertion.

source.place: Proof Step 4, chart specialization: ambient affine-space dimension and quasi-compact complement

proof.text: Apply steps 1-5 to the quasi-compact open immersion $W_U\hookrightarrow T_U$ just checked, with $d=m+\dim B$. The resulting constant is $c_U=2(m+\dim B)$ for every $A_{E,n}$, independently of $n$, and $m+\dim B\leq m+\dim Y$. An empty chart base has empty ambient scheme and complement and contributes no chart to the cover; if retained, it satisfies the condition with $c_U=0$. This is a specialization of the result proved above and uses no admissibility or preservation conclusion from [thm-pur-general-admissibility].

source.place: Proof Step 4, last specialization: uniform chart constants

proof.text: The dimension-zero and curve statements named in the final sentence are the independent computations recorded by [lem-exc-open-complement-known]. That node is cited here solely for this comparison with the previously recorded results; it is not an input to steps 1-7. In particular the present proof does not assume its finite-field special case to establish the separably closed-field result.

Let $k$ be a separably closed field, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring
annihilated by a power of a prime $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$, let
$T$ be a finite-type
$k$-scheme of dimension at most $d$, and let
$j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be a
quasi-compact open immersion.
Then the pair $(V,T)$ satisfies the open-complement condition of
[def-exc-open-complement-bound] with $c=2d$, and it does so for
*every* finite coefficient ring $A$ of that shape at once: both
clauses hold — the vanishing $R^qj_*M=0$ for every $q>2d$ and every
sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules on $V_{\Et}$, and the
constructibility of
$R^qj_*F$ in every degree for every constructible $A$-sheaf $F$ — and
the constant $2d$ depends on $T$ alone, not on $A$. In particular, in
the setting of the global finite-field datum with $k=\Fbar$ and at the
finite coefficient stages $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions], the
condition holds for every $n\geq1$ with the same constant $2d$; for the
chart complements $W_U\subseteq\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ of the assembly
[thm-pur-general-admissibility], where
$d_U+\dim V\leq d_U+\dim Y$, it holds with
$c_U=2(d_U+\dim V)$, again independent of $n$.

proof.text:
The argument is that of [lem-exc-open-complement-known], repeated with
its two hypotheses weakened and its constant tracked; no step of it uses more
about $k$ or about $A$ than the hypotheses of the statement, which is why
the conclusion is uniform in the coefficient ring.

*Step 1: the direct-image input over $k$.* The field $k$ is
separably closed, so both clauses of the direct-image finiteness input
[def-exc-direct-image-input] hold over $k$ by
[thm-exc-direct-image-input-holds], for $N$ the exponent annihilating
$A$ and every finite commutative ring annihilated by $N$.

*Step 2: the constructibility clause.* The open immersion $j$ is
quasi-compact and $T$ is of finite type over $k$, so $j$ is a morphism
of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes; clause (1) of the input
therefore gives, for every constructible $A$-sheaf $F$ on $V_{\Et}$ and
every $q\geq0$, the constructibility of $R^qj_*F$ on $T_{\Et}$. This is
the second clause of the open-complement condition, and it uses
[thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] through that input.

*Step 3: the vanishing clause.* Fix a geometric point
$\bar t\to T$. The strict-henselization stalk formula
[prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] identifies the stalk of
the higher direct image with the cohomology of the open complement over the
strict henselization at $\bar t$,

$$
\bigl(R^qj_*M\bigr)_{\bar t}\cong H^q\bigl(V\times_TT_{(\bar t)},M\bigr),
$$

a filtered colimit of the groups $H^q(V\times_TU,M)$ over the pointed
étale neighbourhoods $U\to T$ of $\bar t$. Each $V\times_TU$ is an
open subscheme of the étale $T$-scheme $U$, hence a finite-type
$k$-scheme of dimension at most $\dim U=\dim T\leq d$; the sheaf $M$ of
$A$-modules is a torsion sheaf of abelian groups, $A$ being finite and
annihilated by a power of $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$, and $k$ is
separably closed with characteristic prime to that power, so clause (2) of
the input gives $H^q(V\times_TU,M)=0$ for every $q>2d$. A filtered
colimit of zero groups is zero, so every geometric stalk of $R^qj_*M$
vanishes for $q>2d$, and the conservativity of geometric stalks
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes the sheaf itself zero.
This is the first clause of the open-complement condition, with $c=2d$.

*Step 4: uniformity in the coefficient ring.* Steps 2 and 3 use of
$A$ exactly its finiteness and the annihilation by a power of a prime
$\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$: the constructibility clause is clause (1)
of the input, whose only coefficient hypothesis is that $A$ is finite and
annihilated by an integer invertible in $k$, and the vanishing clause is
clause (2), which is quantified over all torsion sheaves and mentions no
coefficient ring. The integer $d=\dim T$ likewise depends on the scheme
alone. Hence both clauses hold with the constant $2d$ for every finite ring
$A$ of the stated shape, which is the uniformity assertion. In the global
finite-field datum one has $k=\Fbar$, separably closed with
$\operatorname{char}(k)=p$, and $A_{E,n}$ is annihilated by the power
$\varpi_E^n$ of the prime $\ell\neq p$, so the condition holds at every
stage $n\geq1$ with the constant $2d$; for the chart complement
$W_U$ of the closed subscheme $U\subseteq\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ of
[def-sbc-affine-space] the ambient scheme is of dimension
$d_U+\dim V\leq d_U+\dim Y$, giving $c_U=2(d_U+\dim V)$ independently of
$n$. This is the assertion of the second half of the statement, and the
final sentence records the two independent computations of the same condition
in [lem-exc-open-complement-known].
